description:
In 1994, Mark Messier delivered one of the most iconic performances in NHL history, backing up a bold promise with a clutch Game 6 effort that kept the New York Rangers’ season alive. With the team trailing the New Jersey Devils 3–2 in the Eastern Conference Final, Messier famously declared, “I know we’re going to go in and win Game 6 and bring it back here for Game 7,” according to the New York Daily News. He then made good on his guarantee by scoring a natural hat trick in the third period, leading the Rangers to a 4–2 comeback victory and forcing a decisive Game 7.  
Down 2–1 entering the third period, Messier took control. He tied the game early in the period on the backhand, gave the Rangers the lead driving the net on a rebound, and sealed the game—and his guarantee—with a shorthanded, empty-net goal. That final goal was especially memorable: it began with Messier winning a defensive-zone faceoff during a 6-on-4 penalty kill, then skating up ice to finish the play into the vacant net.    
The Rangers would go on to win Game 7 in double overtime against the Devils and eventually defeat the Vancouver Canucks in the Stanley Cup Final, ending a 54-year championship drought. Messier’s Game 6 performance remains one of the most clutch and iconic moments in NHL playoff history.
